clue.text: She died from a bite in a pectoral manoeuvre

indicators.note: a manoeuvre is a deft rearranging, so the letters of the two words are shifted around

explanation.surface: A grisly anatomy lesson: someone killed by a bite delivered during some move across the chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvre' rearranges A PECTORAL. The Egyptian queen is said to have died from the bite of an asp she held to her breast, which makes 'pectoral' apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian queen famously killed herself by letting a venomous asp bite her.

clue.text: Author of classic tale adapted for a TV screen

indicators.note: a tale adapted for the screen is reworked, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A classic novel's author is reworked for television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges A TV SCREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish novelist wrote Don Quixote, one of the great classic stories of literature.

clue.text: High-flier's notable achievement on course

definitions.meaning: a high-flier here is a big bird of prey soaring aloft
on a golf course, two strokes under par on a hole is a fine score

explanation.surface: A successful person's standout accomplishment along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flier' sounds like an ambitious person; it is the bird. 'course' is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The big raptor is the classic high flier, and in golf the term names a score two under par.

clue.text: Leaves from here to celebrate victory

definitions.text: Leaves from here to celebrate victory

parts.words: Leaves from here to celebrate victory
parts.note: fronds of this tropical plant were waved or worn as tokens of triumph, as in the Palm Sunday story

explanation.surface: Someone departs from this spot to go and toast a win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb (departs); it is the noun, the foliage of the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Its fronds have long been a symbol of triumph, carried by victors in ancient times.

clue.text: Contents of pot as one measure used by cook

indicators.note: what goes into a pot gets stirred and mixed together, so the letters of the words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A recipe direction: what goes in the pot counts as a single measure for the chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contents of' mixes up the letters of POT AS ONE. The surface recalls the tea-making rule of one spoonful per person and one for the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spoon is a standard kitchen unit of quantity in recipes.

clue.text: Unfortunately, king is put over a separate state

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece put over another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning sadly or unfortunately
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A sorry tale of a monarch placed above some separate region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is put over' places K above A in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The 49th US state is cut off from the contiguous states by Canada.

clue.text: Work to break strike? Get lost!

indicators.note: one piece breaks into another, splitting it open and sitting inside it

parts.note: to strike is to hit
OP, short for opus, means a work

explanation.surface: A boss tells a worker who wants to break the strike to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work to break strike' suggests industrial action; the definition is a rude British dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a British slang command telling someone to go away.

clue.text: Time studying at Oxford for boy or girl

definitions.meaning: Oxford University's spring term is named after a saint
a first name given to both males and females

explanation.surface: A period of university study suitable for a son or daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford's three terms are Michaelmas, Hilary and Trinity.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford names its January to March term this way, and it is a forename used for both sexes.

clue.text: Spread widely through volume, as I have contracted

parts.note: per means through or by way of

indicators.note: a contraction drops letters, so the words are shortened as in everyday speech

explanation.surface: Something diffused through a large volume, the speaker confesses having shrunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' turns AS I HAVE into AS I'VE, dropping HA, giving ASIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pervasive is spread throughout, found everywhere.

clue.text: Shrub in season, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, so a same-sounding word is wanted

parts.note: a season is a time of year, as in harvest time

explanation.surface: A bush that is in season, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals a word spoken: TIME sounds like the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: The herb is a small aromatic woody shrub.

clue.text: Royal emblems lost in Algeria

indicators.note: a word that has lost its way and gone astray has its letters in disorder

explanation.surface: Crown jewels go missing in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges ALGERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Crown, sceptre and orb are the symbols of a sovereign's office.

clue.text: Over-sensitive reaction from colleague about amount of work

indicators.note: the colleague goes round, about, the unit of work

parts.note: an ally is a colleague or associate
the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: An overreaction from a co-worker over how much there is to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals a container: the colleague wraps round the unit of work.
explanation.definitionFit: The body's immune system reacts excessively to something harmless, like pollen.

clue.text: Seeing a green, turn off to the side

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: Seeing the golf green, a player turns aside.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is heraldic green. 'Seeing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflect something is to turn it away or aside.

clue.text: Countenance never affected by a flush, for example

definitions.text: Countenance never affected by a flush, for example

parts.words: Countenance never affected by a flush, for example
parts.note: a flush is a red blush and also a card hand; a gambler's expression must stay blank whatever hand is held

explanation.surface: A face that never goes red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flush' reads as blushing; it is also a five-card hand all in one suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A card player's deadpan expression gives nothing away about the hand held.

clue.text: Pill taken before operation — knives etc laid out here

indicators.note: the pill comes before the operation in the answer

parts.note: a tablet is a pill

explanation.surface: A patient takes a pill before surgery, with the scalpels ready on a tray.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to surgical knives; the definition is the cutlery on a dining surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutlery is set out on the surface of a dining table.

clue.text: Working hard to provide existence outside state

indicators.note: the word for existence goes outside, wrapping round, the word for state

parts.note: being means existence
to aver is to state or declare

explanation.surface: Toiling to support life beyond the nation's borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a nation; it is the verb meaning declare. 'outside' signals the word for existence wrapping round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To beaver away is to toil diligently, like the busy rodent.

clue.text: Monarch initially appears to irritate the Church of Scotland

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the synonym for the word before it

parts.note: a king is a monarch
to irk is to irritate

explanation.surface: The king seems to annoy the Scottish church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' works on KING, the synonym of Monarch, not on the printed word, so it gives K.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish national church is commonly called by the Scots word for church.

clue.text: King also high above artist

parts.note: and means also
high above us is up in the sky

explanation.surface: A monarch, and someone lofty, look down on a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high above' is read as IN SKY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian painter was a pioneer of abstract art.

clue.text: She's not quite aristocratic

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls just short, losing its last letter

parts.note: patrician means aristocratic, of noble birth

explanation.surface: A woman who is almost upper-class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last letter N from PATRICIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a female forename, so the pronoun stands for any woman of that name.

clue.text: Dramatist and churchman in leave-taking

indicators.note: the churchman sits in the middle of the word for leave-taking

parts.note: a conge is a formal leave-taking or dismissal
REV, short for reverend, is a churchman

explanation.surface: A playwright and a clergyman saying their farewells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; the conge is an old word for a formal farewell or dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: William Congreve was a Restoration playwright, author of The Way of the World.

clue.text: Brooded about king in game of cards

indicators.note: the word for brooded goes about, around, the king

parts.note: a hen sat on eggs, that is, brooded
K is the card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone sulked over the king in a hand of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brooded' suggests sulking; it is a hen sitting on eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Skat is a three-player German trick-taking card game.

clue.text: Frenchman astride a horse of the old style

indicators.note: the Frenchman sits astride, with legs either side of, the horse

parts.note: Jean is a typical French man's name
a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

explanation.surface: A Frenchman riding a horse in old-fashioned fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astride' signals the Frenchman's name splitting to sit either side of the horse, like a rider's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the era of James I, so it means in an early-seventeenth-century style.

clue.text: Copy diamond, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a duplicate made with old-style transfer paper
diamond is one form of the chemical element, along with graphite

explanation.surface: Imitating a gem, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: A carbon copy was made with sheets of carbon paper; diamond is pure crystallised carbon.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbon is a duplicate document, and diamond is a form of the element.

clue.text: Reptiles that can multiply, too, when necessary

definitions.text: Reptiles that can multiply, too, when necessary

parts.words: Reptiles that can multiply, too, when necessary
parts.note: venomous snakes, also machines or people that sum numbers; repeated sums can multiply

explanation.surface: Snakes that are able to breed as well, when they must.
explanation.walkthrough: Plays on the old joke of snakes that cannot multiply, only add; repeated addition does multiply.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both venomous vipers and devices that sum figures.

clue.text: Name of Pope — or six of them

definitions.text: Name of Pope — or six of them

parts.words: Name of Pope — or six of them
parts.note: eight popes took this name; the sixth, the Borgia pope, is the most notorious, and six of them is the numeral VI

explanation.surface: A papal name, shared by several popes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six of them' points to the sixth holder of the name, Rodrigo Borgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight popes have borne this name, the sixth being the notorious Borgia.

clue.text: Flapping of wings going over motorway

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece going over another sits above it, coming first

parts.note: alar is an adjective meaning of or relating to wings
M is the British abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Birds beating their wings as they fly over a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flapping' looks like wings beating; it is the noun, a state of panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a flap is being in a state of anxious agitation.

clue.text: Writer absorbed in hugging or kissing

indicators.note: absorbed in says the word is soaked up inside the following words, running across them

explanation.surface: An author lost in cuddling or kissing.
explanation.walkthrough: The run crosses huggin-G OR KI-ssing.
explanation.definitionFit: Maxim Gorky, also spelt Gorki, was a Russian novelist and playwright.

clue.text: Tees, for example, in golf club (apart from first)

indicators.note: apart from first means dropping the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a driver is a golf club used off the tee

explanation.surface: Tee pegs at a golf club, except the first hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tees' suggests golf tees; it is the river in north-east England. 'apart from first' drops D.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tees is a waterway in north-east England, one example of the kind.

clue.text: Friendly enquiry about my competence

definitions.meaning: the question whether I am capable, written as three words

explanation.surface: A warm question about one's own abilities.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as AM I ABLE?, it is a question about my ability.
explanation.definitionFit: An amiable person is good-natured and pleasant.

clue.text: Sticks fast or breaks apart

explanation.surface: Something either holds firm or splits.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb has two opposite senses: to cling and to split.
explanation.definitionFit: This verb is a contronym, meaning both adhere and split asunder.

clue.text: Intend to include good Welshwoman

indicators.note: the word for intend takes in, includes, the letter for good

parts.note: to mean is to intend

explanation.surface: Planning to take in a nice woman from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts G inside MEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female forename in Wales.

clue.text: Colour of a flag, perhaps

parts.note: a flag here is a flagstone, a paving slab whose stony hue is a dull blue-grey, not a banner

explanation.surface: The hue of a national banner, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' suggests a banner; it is a flagstone, a stone slab.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagstones are often of a dull bluish-grey rock, giving the shade its name.
